policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the expression as 'his royal pavilion,' while the only note is classed alternative_rendering ('glittering') and therefore cannot decide the qere-versus-ketiv reading; the English does not distinguish the candidates, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.
ASV explicitly has the masculine subject and verb 'he shall come,' distinguishing the masculine qere וּבָא from the feminine ketiv ובאה.
